messages.subject: What does  $mode$mode.status==1000 means?
parts:
Hello everybody,

I read in this post https://goo.gl/16sJJ2  that mode$mode.status==0 its OK, larger values are still useful, but that mode.status==1000 means: Hessian is not SPD.

My focus is on predictions and I got 1000 for my best significant model that includes just the spatial random effect. 

What does this mean?

Does this means that the stochastic partial differential equation approach is not suitable when using just the spatial component and I have to select the best significant model with mode.status==1000?

Many thanks in advance

Miguel

messages.author: 3eab71733027a24a
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] What does  $mode$mode.status==1000 means?
parts:
On Thu, 2017-07-06 at 10:12 -0700, Mike wrote:
> Hello everybody,
>
> I read in this post https://goo.gl/16sJJ2  that mode$mode.status==0
> its OK, larger values are still useful, but that mode.status==1000
> means: Hessian is not SPD.
>
> My focus is on predictions and I got 1000 for my best significant
> model that includes just the spatial random effect. 
>
> What does this mean?
>
> Does this means that the stochastic partial differential equation
> approach is not suitable when using just the spatial component and I
> have to select the best significant model with mode.status==1000?

it simply means that the found hessian at the mode has the wrong sign.
this can be due to two things. 1: the mode is not found sufficiently
accurate enough, or 2: the numerical approximation for the hessian
fail.

you may try to restart in these cases, like
r = inla.rerun(r)

this is the most likely reason. moreover, this usually happens when the
log posterior is almost flat, hence its back the model that is not very
informative wrt some or one of the parameters. more informative priors
would help.

Best
H

--
Håvard Rue
he...@r-inla.org
